description: F-TAX-003: `TaxProfile.fromData` coerced where every neighbour refuses. `taxationMethod` was `data.taxationMethod === 'cash' ? 'cash' : 'accrual'` and `vatPeriod` was `=== 'monthly' ? 'monthly' : 'quarterly'`, so a typo, a null or an object all arrived as a valid-looking profile that books differently, and nothing reported it. Same shape as the `direction` default that booked an incoming invoice fully inverted (IMPL-013) and as the operation input that was dropped rather than rejected (F-9) — except this one decides whether VAT falls due on invoice or on payment, which is the difference between two correct-looking sets of books. It is ordinary caller input, not a value object built from a trusted internal source: `fromData` is fed from an embedding's configuration file, which is exactly where a typo lives. `yearly` comes with it as a third filing period, because § 18 Abs. 2 UStG lets a small enough business file once a year and a caller who wrote it silently got quarterly. The period is descriptive — it records which window a tenant files in and does not select one in `vatReturn`. Reported by an embedding application as its F-19.

steps.comment: Yearly filing is a real thing to want — and a caller who wrote it used to get quarterly, with no error and no warning.
setTaxProfile returns the serialized profile, which is where the stored period becomes visible.
"kasse" is not "cash". It used to fall through to accrual — the tenant then taxed on invoice while its configuration said on payment.
A missing letter in the filing period was quarterly, silently.
An explicit null is a caller mistake too — absent is a default, null is a statement.
